svg.aria-label: BCBC 2024 Article 9.10.9.18 Separation of Storage Garages
svg.title: BCBC 2024 · 9.10.9.18 Separation of Storage Garages
svg.text: BCBC 2024 · DIVISION B · PART 9 HOUSING AND SMALL BUILDINGS · SECTION 9.10 FIRE PROTECTION
Separation of Storage Garages

g.text: Storage garage: fire separation of at
Storage garage for 5 motor vehicles or
fewer: fire separation of at least 1 h
Garage serving only its own dwelling unit:
part of that dwelling unit, no fire separation
an effective barrier to gas and exhaust fumes

svg.text: WHAT THE CODE REQUIRES
A storage garage is separated from other occupancies by a fire
separation having not less than a 1.5 h fire-resistance rating
Except as provided in Sentences (2) and (3).
Storage garages containing 5 motor vehicles or fewer are
separated from other occupancies by a fire separation of not
less than 1 h
Except as permitted in Sentence (3).
A storage garage serving only the dwelling unit to which it is
attached or in which it is built is considered part of that
dwelling unit, and the fire separation of Sentence (2) need not
be provided between them
Where a storage garage is attached to or built into a building
of residential occupancy
(a) an air barrier system conforming to Subsection 9.25.3. is
installed between the garage and the rest of the building as an
effective barrier to gas and exhaust fumes, and (b) every door between
them conforms to Article 9.10.13.15. Except as in Sentence (5). See
Where membrane materials provide the required airtightness in
the air barrier system, all joints are sealed and structurally
supported
The door is tight fitting, weather-stripped and self-closing, and the
doorway is not in a room intended for sleeping.
The barrier keeps carbon monoxide and gasoline fumes out of the
dwelling unit. Where the garage is open to the attic over the dwelling
unit, a gas-tight ceiling barrier also protects. Masonry walls should
have two coats of sealer or plaster, or gypsum board on the garage
side, with all joints sealed.
Drawn: a slice, two buildings and a close-up with boards left off. Red: rated fire separations. Blue sheet: air barrier membrane.
Source: BCBC 2024, Division B, Article 9.10.9.18. (page 9-72)
